anchors.paper_title: Large-scale training data enhances silent speech decoding with around-ear EEG
anchors.reason: Same authors (Inoue, Hatakeyama, Kita, Sasai); paper reports collecting around-ear EEG during silent/vocalized speech from 24 participants, matching this EEG-speech dataset with overt speech task.

metadata.methods_description: Participants vocalized visually presented text (speechopen task) while EEG and audio were recorded. EEG was stored in EDF format and vocal recordings as WAV files, organized by session (recording date) and run.

citation_details.title: Brain-to-Language Decoding: Paradigms, Signals, Methods, Evaluation, Practical Use and Beyond
citation_details.author: Yiqian Yang, Yiqun Duan, Chenyu Liu, Yiqi Wang, Xinliang Zhou, Chin-Teng Lin, Yu Zhang
citation_details.abstract: Brain-to-language decoding translates neural activity associated with language production, internal speech and perception into linguistic or expressive outputs. It offers a route to restoring communication after speech loss and a means of studying how the brain represents language. Advances in neural recording and representation learning have expanded the field from constrained recognition and acoustic reconstruction to text generation, streaming personalised speech and facial animation. This survey synthesises these developments across invasive and non-invasive measurements. We connect Articulated, Inner and Perceived paradigms to the neural populations they engage, the representations available to decoders and the outputs those representations can support. We examine model development, public resources and the evolution of evaluation, and compare published performance and communication costs within their reported protocols. citation_details.title: Predicting Cognitive Tasks from Single-Channel EEG through Task-Semantic Alignment
citation_details.author: Ryota Kanai
citation_details.abstract: Studies of data scaling in electroencephalography (EEG) and related noninvasive recordings suggest that simple wearable devices could eventually reveal more about cognitive states. However, publicly available EEG data are difficult to combine. Different laboratories record different tasks, participants, and devices. Task-agnostic self-supervised learning can exploit such data, but representations learned only with EEG signals have not consistently produced feature representations that are directly effective for decoding the cognitive state. We therefore aimed to incorporate task information by embedding experimental instructions, stimuli and response demands in a common semantic space, and trained an EEG encoder to align signals from a single anterior--posterior differential channel with those task vectors. citation_details.title: AESSI: An Around-Ear Silent Speech Interface for Cross-Day Online Reuse without Test-Day Calibration
citation_details.author: Xiran Xu, Mochu Dong, Yujie Yan, Chenxi Wang, Yu Jiao, Jing Chen
citation_details.abstract: Silent speech interfaces (SSIs) enable private communication without audible speech and may support people with post-stroke dysarthria. Everyday reuse requires articulation-related representations that generalize across days despite sensor repositioning and physiological changes. We present AESSI, an around-ear SSI using masked-context representation pretraining (MCRP): a student predicts teacher representations from masked time-frequency inputs to encourage robustness to recording variability. We collected 44 electrophysiological recordings from 24 participants for 25 everyday Mandarin sentences. With six participants' complete final recordings held out, AESSI achieved 92.24 percent mean accuracy without test-day calibration. AESSI exceeded the best adapted baseline by 50.57 percentage points. At least 21 days after each participant's last recording, five participants each completed 50 independently randomized online tests without calibration, achieving 98.0 percent overall accuracy.

citation_details.title: A Decade of cEEGrid: What the Around-the-Ear Array Can and Cannot Measure
citation_details.author: Bin Gou, Zikang Song, Mangor Pedersen, Paul F. Sowman
citation_details.abstract: Abstract Objective. cEEGrid, a C-shaped flexible electrode array worn around the ear, has been applied across auditory, cognitive, brain-computer interface, clinical, and sleep applications. We ask what the array can and cannot measure, why, and what separates laboratory feasibility from real-world use. Approach. In this scoping review with a quantitative methodological audit, we reviewed 67 studies using cEEGrid or its derivative hardware, examining acquisition hardware, analysis algorithms, and channel-naming, montage and re-referencing conventions, and comparing reported performance against simultaneously recorded cap-EEG where paired data existed. Main results. cEEGrid’s spatial sensitivity depends on the position and orientation of the source relative to the array, rather than electrode-to-source distance alone. citation_details.title: Bio-integrated systems for silent speech recognition: from advanced bioplatforms to machine learning-assisted biosignal decoding
citation_details.author: Penghao Dong, Yuanqing Song, Yizong Li, Petar M. Djurić, Shanshan Yao
citation_details.abstract: Silent speech interfaces decode intended speech from physiological signals without the need for vocalized sound. These systems provide an alternative modality to voice-based spoken communication, addressing limitations posed by physiological constraints and environmental interferences. This review presents a comprehensive overview of bio-integrated systems for silent speech recognition, with emphasis on their physiological relevance, state-of-the-art hardware designs, signal characteristics, and machine learning (ML)-assisted speech decoding pipelines. Based on the level of physical intrusion into the body, bio-integrated speech interfaces can be categorized into epidermal, intraoral, and surgically embedded systems. Each modality captures distinct physiological signals involved in speech production.
